5RQJ: Pankaj = mud. Nigharat hai = keeps sinking. Kaadh = pulling out. Kadhavaigo = brings to the bank.
A person keeps sinking into the bog of attachment (to Maya); the Guru pulls out the person sinking (in this bog) and brings them to the bank.
The mortal beings are sinking in the swamp of emotional attachment; the Guru lifts them up, and saves them from sinking.
The mortal is sinking in the mire of worldly love and the Guru saves him from sinking.
The mortal who keeps sinking into the (pank) mud of attachment — the Guru will pull out the one sinking in that bog, as is fit.
83PW: Traah traah = save me, save me. Haathee = hand. De = giving. ||4||
Those who come to (the Guru's) shelter crying "Save me, save me!" — the Guru gives them His hand and pulls them out (of the bog of attachment to Maya). ||4||
Crying, "Save me! Save me!", the humble come to His Sanctuary; the Guru reaches out His Hand, and lifts them up. ||4||
When man repeating "Save me, save me" comes into the Guru's refuge, the Guru extends his hand and pulls him out.
When the servants come to the Guru's shelter saying "Protect us, protect us!", then the Guru, the form of compassion or the form of teaching, will give His (haathee) arm and pull them out. ||4||
XC7V: Supnantar = (supan-antar) the inner dream, the dream of the mind, the wandering of the mind. {Note: the difference between the words 'antar' and 'antari' is worth remembering (see stanza 8, 'rid antari').} Sabh = the whole (world). Khilavaigo = (Parmatma Himself) is making (it) play.
This world is (the root of) the wandering of (a person's) mind; the whole world is (just a kind of) play (to keep beings occupied). (Parmatma Himself) is making (beings) play this game.
The whole world is like a game in a dream, all a game. God plays and causes the game to be played.
The whole world is like the game of a dream. The Lord, of Himself, causes the whole game and play to be played.

Just as whatever thing appears in a dream is false, so is the whole world; and just as a juggler's show is false and scatters in an instant, so the whole world is a juggler's show, and all of it will scatter.
W0N2: Laaha = profit, earnings. Lai = taking. Chaalahu = set out (from the world). Paidha = having received a robe of honour, with honour. Javaigo = goes. ||5||

(In this game, Parmatma's) Name (alone) is the profit. Through the Guru's teaching, earn this profit and go. (The person who earns this profit and leaves here) goes into Parmatma's presence with honour. ||5||
So earn the Profit of the Naam by following the Guru's Teachings; you shall go to the Court of the Lord in robes of honor. ||5||
If man departs, reaping the Name's profit under the Guru's instruction, he goes to the Lord's court robed with glory.
So, O brother! Through the Guru's teaching, take the profit of the Name with you; you will go into Hari's court wearing the robe of honour. ||5||
40DL: Karai karavai = doing and having done, doing at every moment. Aan = bringing. Jamavaigo = sows.
The person who keeps saying "I, I" all their life keeps bringing in the coals of sin and sowing them (in the field of their mind).
They act in egotism, and make others act in egotism; they collect and gather up the blackness of sin.
In ego man acts, in ego he makes others act and thus brings and amasses he, the blackness of sins in ego.
Whoever does deeds with egotism and possessiveness, and in ego has others do deeds, will come and pile up the coals of sin.
49NU: Kaal = death. Jo = those which. Koile = sins. Beeje = have been sown. Khavlavaigo = makes one taste the fruit. ||6||
When death comes, (those sown and earned sins) become painful (but what can be done then?). The coals of sin that have been sown (committed all through life) — their fruit has to be eaten. ||6||
And when death comes, they suffer in agony; they must eat what they have planted. ||6||
When death comes, he suffers pain because the man must eat that, what he had sown.
When death came upon their head, all the sins became painful, because whatever the being sows, Parmeshar makes them eat — meaning as they act, so they will reap. ||6||
4GMZ: Santahu = O saints! Sanchahu = gather. Lai = taking. Chale = set out. Pat = honour. Pavaigo = puts in the lap, gives.
O saints! Keep gathering the wealth of Parmatma's Name. (Those who) set out taking the provisions (of the Name to spend on life's journey), (Parmatma) gives (them) honour.
O Saints, gather the Wealth of the Lord's Name; if you depart after packing these provisions, you shall be honored.
O saints, amass the wealth of the Lord's Name; if you depart by taking this viaticum, you shall obtain honour.
O saints! Gather the wealth of Ram's Name; whoever takes the provisions with them will gain honour.
PFV0: Khai = eating (oneself). Kharach = spending, sharing (with others). Devahi = (the saints) give. Dede = while giving. Tot = shortage, lack. ||7||
Those people, (using this wealth of the Name themselves) freely, also share it widely (with others); in sharing this wealth of Hari's Name, it never runs short. ||7||
So eat, spend, consume and give abundantly; the Lord will give - there will be no deficiency. ||7||
Eat, expend and bestow it abundantly and God will so give you, that there shall be no deficiency.
That one will (khai kharach) chant themselves and teach others abundantly; in giving Hari's Name, they will never run short. ||7||
AT6X: (O brother!) This wealth of the Name is found by taking the Guru's shelter. The person in whose heart this wealth of the Name dwells —
The wealth of the Lord's Name is deep within the heart. In the Sanctuary of the Guru, this wealth is found.
The wealth of the Lord's Name is within the mind, Seeking the Guru's refuge, you shall obtain this wealth.
The wealth of Ram's Name is within the heart itself, but this wealth is found by attaining the Guru's shelter.
5FE9: Deenee = gave (the gift of the wealth of the Name). Kar = showing. Daalad = poverty. Bhanj = breaking, destroying, ending. ||8||5||
the person to whom Parmatma, in His kindness, gives the gift of the wealth of the Name — O Nanak! — they remove every pain, end (spiritual) poverty, and stay absorbed in the Name. ||8||5||
O Nanak, God has been kind and compassionate; He has blessed me. Removing pain and poverty, He has blended me with Himself. ||8||5||
Nanak, showing His mercy and compassion, the Lord has blest me with this wealth and removing my misery has blended me with Himself.
Sri Guru ji says: when the Guru, the form of kindness, in kindness gave the treasure of Ram's Name, then, destroying all pain and poverty, the soul will merge into Parmeshar. ||8||5||
99X2: Man = the mind (of the person). Dhiavaigo = meditates (on Hari's Name).
(The person whose) mind, taking the Guru's shelter, keeps remembering Parmatma's Name —
O mind, seek the Sanctuary of the True Guru, and meditate.
O my soul, enter you into the sanctuary of the True Guru and meditate on your Lord.
O brother! The seeker whose mind meditates on the shelter of the True Guru —
XGVB: Hiran = (hiranya) gold. Sang paras = together with (touching) the philosopher's stone. Gun paras ko = the quality of the philosopher's stone. ||1|| Rahau ||
(they become of lofty life through the touch of Prabhu's feet, just as) iron becomes gold (touching) the philosopher's stone; the quality of the stone's touch comes into it. ||1|| Rahau ||
Iron is transformed into gold by touching the philosopher's stone; it takes on its qualities. ||1||Pause||
As iron is transmuted into gold by touching the philosopher's stone, so do the virtues of the invaluable personality of the Guru enter into his disciples. Pause.
just as iron meeting the philosopher's stone becomes (hiran) gold, so the quality of the stone will come into them — meaning the excellent seeker becomes able to purify others. ||1|| Rahau ||
6FX9: Jo laagai = the person who touches.
The Guru (too) is a very great Being; (the Guru too) is a philosopher's stone. The person who clings (to the Guru's feet) gains (the highest) fruit,
The True Guru, the Great Primal Being, is the philosopher's stone. Whoever is attached to Him receives fruitful rewards.
The True Guru, the supreme person, is the philosopher's stone. Whosoever is attached to him, he gathers the fruit.
The True Guru, the great Being, is the form of the philosopher's stone; whoever clings to Him — meaning meets Him — will gain the fruit of spiritual knowledge.
V3SG: Updes = through the teaching. Tare prahilada = Prahlad and many others crossed over. Paij = honour. ||1||
just as through the blessing of the Guru's teaching Prahlad (and many others) crossed over. The Guru (surely) keeps the honour of His (servant). ||1||
Just as Prahlaad was saved by the Guru's Teachings, the Guru protects the honor of His servant. ||1||
Just as Prahlad saved by the Guru's instruction, similarly the Guru protects the honour of all his attendants.
Just as Prahlad crossed over through the Guru's teaching, so the Guru will keep the honour of the servant. ||1||
Q6RR: Neeko = good, most excellent. Gur bachnee = through the Guru's words. Amrit = the water of the Name that gives spiritual life.
Know for certain that the Guru's word is (most) excellent. Through the blessing of the Guru's words, (a person) gains the Name that gives spiritual life.
The Word of the True Guru is the most Sublime and Noble Word. Through the Guru's Word, the Ambrosial Nectar is obtained.
The True Guru's word if the sublime word. By the Guru's word, the Name-Nectar is obtained.
Of all words, the True Guru's word is the finest; through the Guru's words the being will gain the nectar of the Name.
ZQY7: Ambareek = Ambareek. Amra pad = the undying state, the level where spiritual death cannot touch. Mukh bachan = the words of the mouth. Satgur mukh bachan = the words from the Guru's mouth. Dhiavaigo = utters. ||2||
(Whoever) settles the Word uttered by the Guru in their heart (gains a lofty spiritual life), just as Ambareek attained the spiritual level where spiritual death cannot touch. ||2||
Ambreek the king was blessed with the status of immortality, meditating on the Word of the True Guru. ||2||
Whosoever reflects on the Supreme True Guru's word, he is blessed with the immortal status like Amrik, the King.
Whoever takes the True Guru's word and meditates on Parmeshar will reach the undying state, like Ambareek. ||2||
16B3: Man = in the mind. Bhaee = felt good. Sudha = amrit, nectar. Sudha sudha kar = firmly believing (it) to be the giver of spiritual life.
The person to whose mind staying in the Guru's shelter becomes pleasing — they, firmly believing (the Guru's word) to be the giver of spiritual life, keep (it) settled within.
The Sanctuary, the Protection and Sanctuary of the True Guru is pleasing to the mind. It is sacred and pure - meditate on it.
The True Guru's refuge, yea, his refuge is pleasing to my mind. Deeming the Name-Nectar immaculate, meditate I on it.
Those in whose mind, of all shelters, the True Guru's shelter is pleasing will, for the (sudha) nectar of the Name, meditate on the Guru, the moon that is (sudha kar) the mine of nectar.
E51D: Daial deen = merciful to the humble. Marag panth = the path of spiritual life. ||3||
The Guru is merciful to the humble; the Guru shows the path of union with Parmatma. ||3||
The True Guru has become Merciful to the meek and the poor; He has shown me the Path, the Way to the Lord. ||3||
The True Guru has become merciful to me, the meek one and he has shown me the way and path of God.
When the True Guru is merciful to the humble, then on the road of the world the Guru will show Hari's path. ||3||
26PG: Se = those people. Thaape = were established, were given honour.
Those who take the Guru's shelter receive honour; Parmatma Himself comes to protect them.
Those who enter the Sanctuary of the True Guru are firmly established; God comes to protect them.
They, who enter the sanctuary of the True Guru, are blessed with glory and the Lord comes to protect them.
Those who have fallen into the True Guru's shelter are (thaape) established in the state of liberation; Prabhu Himself will come to protect them.
ECEU: Ko = anyone. Sar = arrow. Sandhai = takes aim. Ulto = turned back. ||4||
If anyone shoots an arrow at those servants, that arrow turns back and strikes that very person. ||4||
If someone aims an arrow at the Lord's humble servant, it will turn around and hit him instead. ||4||
If some one aims an arrow on the Lord's slave, turning back, it hits him ultimately.
Whoever aims an arrow at the servants — meaning whoever wishes ill to the saints — Hari will turn it back and strike them with it; meaning the ill will befall them alone. ||4||
JJR5: Sar = pool, lake. Har sar = the pool in which the stream of the water of Hari's Name flows; the holy company. Har sar sevahi = (the people who) serve the holy company. Maan = honour.
The people who always keep the support of the holy company — Parmatma has them given honour in His presence.
Those who bathe in the Sacred Pool of the Lord, Har, Har, Har, Har, Har, are blessed with honor in His Court.
They, who bathe in the Name-tank of the Lord God Master, yea, the Lord God, they are blessed with honour in His Court.
Hari's pool is the true company; those who go into it and serve the Name "Hari Hari" of Hari, the remover of pains — Hari will have them given honour in His court.
ALBU: Gurmat = taking the Guru's teaching. Gal = to the neck. Mil = meeting. Mel = into union, with Himself. ||5||
The people who always walk on the Guru's teaching and remember Parmatma's Name — Parmatma meets them in an embrace and makes them one with Himself. ||5||
Those who meditate on the Guru's Teachings, the Guru's Instructions, the Guru's Wisdom, are united in the Lord's Union; He hugs them close in His Embrace. ||5||
He, who by Guru's instructions, Guru's directions, and Guru's teaching meditates on God; him, the Lord hugs to His bosom and unites in His union.

The Guru is (gur) worthy of worship; of all doctrines, the Guru's doctrine is theirs. The person who meditates on it in their own mind meets Hari in an embrace and will join others in the union. ||5||
G3SA: Gurmukh = the person who takes the Guru's shelter; the Guru's shelter. Gur parchai = through the Guru's pleasure.

For the person who stays facing the Guru, the Guru's shelter is itself the Naad; the Guru's shelter is itself the Veda. The person who stays in the Guru's shelter gains the Guru's pleasure and remembers Hari's Name.
The Guru's Word is the Sound-current of the Naad, The Guru's Word is the wisdom of the Vedas; coming in contact with the Guru, meditate on the Naam.
The Supreme Guru is the celestial strain for him and the Supreme Guru, the Vedas; by pleasing the Guru, he ponders on the Lord's Name.
The (naad) word from the Guru's mouth, which the Gurmukh has known as the giver of liberation (bed), — that person, through the Guru's (parchai) teaching, will meditate on the Name.
0T5K: Roopo = the very form. Hovai = becomes. Pooj = worship, honour. ||6||
That person becomes the very form of Parmatma; Parmatma (too) has them honoured (everywhere). ||6||
In the Image of the Lord, Har, Har, one becomes the Embodiment of the Lord. The Lord makes His humble servant worthy of worship. ||6||
Contemplating the Beauteous Lord God, man becomes the embodiment of the Lord. The Lord makes the world worship such a slave of His.
Chanting the Name "Hari Hari" and meditating on Hari's form, they become Hari's form, and in the world Hari will make that servant of His worthy of worship. ||6||
UD9S: Saakat nar = people cut off from Parmatma. Keea = made. Te = those people (plural). Bemukh = those who keep their face turned from the Guru. Bharmavaigo = keeps in wandering.
People cut off from Parmatma do not make the Guru (their support); they keep their face turned away from the Guru, (and) Prabhu keeps them in wandering,
The faithless cynic does not submit to the True Guru; the Lord makes the non-believer wander in confusion.
The perverse person comes not into the True Guru's fold. Such a non-believer, God makes wander in species.
The saakat person has not taken up a True Guru; Hari will make that faithless one wander through the life-forms.
115P: Suan = dog. Bikh = the poison that brings spiritual death. Karang = on the carcass. ||7||

(within them) the wave of greed keeps rising; (this wave) is like the nature of a dog. (As a dog) goes to a carcass (and eats it with delight, so the person driven by the wave of greed) stays clinging to the poison of Maya, which brings spiritual death. ||7||
The waves of greed are like packs of dogs. The poison of Maya sticks to the body-skeleton. ||7||
The wave of avarice is the association of a cur, It attaches one to the Skeleton of the poisonous mammon.
The wave of greed — that is, greed — is a (suan) dog. Whoever has kept its company, by the force of Maya He will fix that greedy one on the carcasses that are the sense-objects born of Maya. ||7||
MW7J: Taarak = the one who carries across. Lag = clinging.
Parmatma's Name carries the whole world across. (The person who) remains in the holy company and remembers Hari's Name (crosses the world-ocean).
The Lord's Name is the Saving Grace of the whole world; join the Sangat, and meditate on the Naam.
The Lord's Name is the emancipation of the whole world and associating with the society of saints, one contemplates the Name.
Ram's Name carries the whole world across, but only whoever joins the true company will meditate on the Name.
NZU8: Prabh mere = O my Prabhu! Raakh = keeping. Samavaigo = keeps absorbed (in Himself). ||8||6|| Chhaka 1 ||
O Nanak! (Pray:) O my Prabhu! Keep (me too in the holy company). (Parmatma,) keeping (a person) in the holy company, keeps (them) absorbed (in Himself). ||8||6|| Chhaka 1 ||
O my God, please protect and preserve Nanak in the Sat Sangat, the True Congregation; save him, and let him merge in You. ||8||6|| First Set of Six ||
O my Lord keep, sustains and maintain You, Nanak, in the saints congregation, so that he may be absorbed in You.

Sri Guru ji says: O my Prabhu, able to protect! Whoever You have kept in the true company will alone merge into You, so protect me. ||8||6|| ☬ Because it joins together six hymns, it is called a "chhaka" (set of six). ||1||
